posts.title: How I'd set a minimum price before matching the guy down the street
posts.text: Don't start from "what the guy down the street charges." Start from what the stop actually costs, then set a floor, then check the market. Build a fully loaded cost for each job: on-site labor (wage plus payroll burden), windshield time, mileage, materials, and a slice of weekly overhead (insurance, phone, software, unpaid admin, equipment). The minimum price at your target margin is: Minimum price = Fully loaded cost ÷ (1 − target margin) EXAMPLE only — not a recommended price and not a... posts.text: In my state, only companies with 10 or more employees are required to pay sick leave. I have one full time and one part time employee. posts.text: Hey guys, Curious how everyone handles inspections before giving a quote. For smaller jobs, a quick walkthrough is usually enough.
